arm: Singular extensions (NEW -- the largest unclaimed Phase 9 item)
verdict: SHELVED as POSITIVE BUT UNRESOLVED: +4.3 Elo, 95% CI [-11.3, +20.0].
idea: If the TT move is much better than every alternative, the position hinges on it and searching it a ply deeper is worth more than spreading the same effort over siblings. Establish singularity by searching everything EXCEPT the TT move at reduced depth against a window just below the TT score; if they all fail low, extend.

implementation.gate: depth >= SE_MIN_DEPTH (8), not in check, beta inside the mate window, TT entry present with depth + 3 >= depth, bound Lower or Exact, |score| inside the mate window.
implementation.probe: alphabeta(board, (depth-1)/2, target-1, target) with target = tt_score - 2*depth, the TT move excluded.
implementation.exclusion_mechanism: An `excluded_move` field CONSUMED by `take()` as the first statement of alphabeta -- before even the depth==0 early return -- so it applies to exactly one node and cannot leak into a child.

correctness_properties_verified_before_s.no_leak: Instrumented probe reported leaked_exclusion=false after every test search. This was the failure mode of most concern: an exclusion escaping into child nodes would silently corrupt whole subtrees, exactly like the root-split defect found the same morning.
correctness_properties_verified_before_s.no_tt_poisoning: An excluded search describes a position with a move removed, so both the TT cutoff on entry and the TT store on exit are suppressed. Using the entry would also be circular -- it was written with the excluded move available.
correctness_properties_verified_before_s.single_legal_move: If the excluded move is the only legal move, nothing is searched and `best` would still hold the -MATE_SCORE sentinel, claiming a forced mate that does not exist. Now returns a fail-low, which is also semantically correct: no alternative beat the window because there were none, which is precisely what makes the move singular.
correctness_properties_verified_before_s.rate_is_normal: 10-31% of probes yielding an extension is the usual range for this heuristic.

matein3_is_STRUCTURALLY_blind_here.evidence: Both a depth-7 and a depth-9 run were BYTE-IDENTICAL to the stub (10011374 and 61832779).
matein3_is_STRUCTURALLY_blind_here.reason: Every position in the suite is a mate window, and the gate deliberately disables singular extensions when |score| is near MATE_SCORE -- extending inside a forced mate is pointless. The identical node counts confirm the GATE works; they say nothing about the feature.
matein3_is_STRUCTURALLY_blind_here.note: This is the same category as the Lazy SMP change, and unlike H2 continuation history: an effect the suite cannot express, rather than a small effect it can.

measurement.harness: compare_play, 400 games, 1000 ms/move, paired openings, seed 20260820, 11 workers
measurement.reading: The -0.28 ply is EXPECTED and not a defect: extensions buy selective depth on critical lines by spending nominal depth everywhere else. The trade happened as designed and netted positive; it simply does not resolve at 400 games.

the_bundle_opportunity.observation: IIR and singular extensions BOTH screened at exactly +4.3 Elo with intervals spanning zero, on the same day against the same baseline.
the_bundle_opportunity.why_they_compose: They are opposite halves of the same idea -- spend depth where it matters. IIR REDUCES nodes with no trustworthy first guess; SE EXTENDS nodes whose answer hinges on one move. Neither competes with the other for the same nodes.
the_bundle_opportunity.the_arithmetic: If the effects are additive, a bundle is ~+9 Elo, which is far more resolvable than +4.3. Resolving a 4 Elo effect needs roughly 4,000 games (~10 h at this cadence); a 9 Elo effect needs roughly 800-1,200.
the_bundle_opportunity.the_caveat: Additivity is an assumption, not a measurement, and bundling breaks per-arm attribution. It should be run as a DECLARED bundle -- screen the pair, then confirm at 1000 games -- not as a way of rescuing two arms that individually failed.
the_bundle_opportunity.recommendation: This is the cheapest remaining search Elo and it is a well-defined ~2 h experiment. It is the first thing to try when compute is next available.

caveats: 400-game screen only; no confirmation, since the lower bound did not clear zero.
SE_MIN_DEPTH (8) and the 2*depth margin are standard choices, not tuned. Both are untested headroom.
The probe depth (depth-1)/2 is a common formula but was not swept.
Modern engines apply double/negative extensions based on how far the probe fails low; this implementation extends by exactly one ply or not at all.
Measured against a baseline carrying both Lazy SMP and log-log LMR promoted the same day.
